title: One throwable Refusal + answerFailure: lib errors carry the code, not routes
acceptance: new Refusal("POSTING_CLOSED", 410) -> instanceof Error AND instanceof Refusal; .code === "POSTING_CLOSED", .status === 410; with no detail argument .message === REFUSAL_ERRORS.POSTING_CLOSED (the log line is never empty)
answerFailure(new Refusal("POSTING_CLOSED", 410), "api:x", "DEVCASE_SUBMIT_FAILED") -> status 410, body { error: REFUSAL_ERRORS.POSTING_CLOSED, code: "POSTING_CLOSED" }, console.error NOT called

answerFailure(new Error("SQLITE_CORRUPT: /abs/data/kp.sqlite"), "api:x", "DEVCASE_SUBMIT_FAILED") -> status 500, body { error: STORE_ERRORS.DEVCASE_SUBMIT_FAILED, code: "DEVCASE_SUBMIT_FAILED" }; serialized body contains neither "SQLITE" nor "kp.sqlite"; console.error called once with "[api:x] DEVCASE_SUBMIT_FAILED"

Operator detail stays off the wire: answerFailure(new Refusal("ATS_FIELD_MAP_INVALID", 400, { detail: 'unknown mapped field "foo"' }), ...) -> 400 with code ATS_FIELD_MAP_INVALID; the body does not contain "unknown mapped field"; the detail is logged at info level

Extra data rides beside the code: new Refusal("PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE", 413, { extra: { maxBytes: 1024 } }) answered -> body has maxBytes: 1024 alongside code, exactly as jsonRefusal(code, status, extra) does today

Migrated classes are Refusals: new PostingClosedError(), new PortabilityError(<code>, 409, msg), new AtsConnectionError(msg, "ATS_PROVIDER_UNKNOWN"-class code), new AtsConnectionStaleError(msg), new AtsFieldMapError(msg) are each instanceof Refusal with the code/status their route answered before this change (410, error.status, 400, 409, 400)

Tree guard (refusal.test.ts walks app/_lib): 0 classes that declare a `code` typed RefusalErrorCode (or assign a REFUSAL_ERRORS key) while extending bare Error; and app/_lib/refusal.ts imports nothing from next/server (source assertion), so any lib module can throw it without pulling NextResponse

The six migrated route catches collapse to one answer: devcase inbound/submit/session-submit and workspace export/import each end in `return answerFailure(error, "api:<route>", "<STORE_CODE>")` with no `instanceof PostingClosedError|PortabilityError` branch left (source assertion); ats/connections keeps ONLY its AtsConnectionStaleError branch (it attaches the live row read at catch time) and answers the rest via answerFailure
premise: app/_lib/api-response.ts:1890-1896 — jsonRefusal(code, status, extra) is the refusal responder; app/_lib/api-response.ts:1923-1926 — safeJsonError(err, route, code) is the store responder. Nothing joins them: every route decides which one applies itself.

app/_lib/ats/connections-store.ts:46-56 — AtsConnectionError already carries `readonly code: RefusalErrorCode`; app/_lib/ats/field-map.ts:129-139 — AtsFieldMapError carries `readonly code: RefusalErrorCode = "ATS_FIELD_MAP_INVALID"`; app/_lib/db-portability.ts:25-34 — PortabilityError carries code + status. Three hand-made versions of the same shape, none shared.

app/_lib/distribution.ts:97-102 — PostingClosedError carries NO code; three routes each hard-code the mapping: app/api/devcase/inbound/route.ts:122-124, app/api/devcase/submit/route.ts:75-77, app/api/devcase/session/[id]/submit/route.ts:158 (`jsonRefusal("POSTING_CLOSED", 410)`).

app/api/workspace/export/route.ts:68 and app/api/workspace/import/route.ts:98 — identical `if (error instanceof PortabilityError) return jsonRefusal(error.code, error.status)`; app/api/workspace/import/import-body-limit.test.ts:68 pins that line by regex.

app/api/ats/connections/route.ts:77-80 — `error instanceof AtsConnectionError || error instanceof AtsFieldMapError` then console.info + jsonRefusal(error.code, 400): the refusal/store split re-derived at the route.

Two more bespoke refusal-vs-store classifiers exist for the same decision: app/api/matrix/matrix-error-code.ts:15-21 (MatrixAnswer {kind:'refusal'|'store'}) and app/api/extract-text/route.ts:44 (ExtractAnswer).
Scale: 30 distinct `instanceof <X>Error` checks across app/api (grep), over 43 `class …Error extends Error` declarations in 39 non-test files under app/.

The cost of the route-level mapping is a live leak: app/api/jobs/[id]/candidates/route.ts:99-100 answers PipelineError with `{ error: error.message, ... }` — listed on LEAK_CEILING in app/api/error-response-contract.test.ts.
rollback: Additive then substitutive: refusal.ts + answerFailure land first (unused = inert); each migrated class keeps its name, constructor signature and code/status fields, so reverting the class commits restores `extends Error` without touching callers, and reverting a route commit restores its explicit instanceof branch. No wire shape changes — the same code/status/body reaches every client — so the series reverts cleanly in any order.
runner_up: A validated request-body door: readJsonWithLimit + a schema check that answers coded refusals, retiring the 117 route files that still call raw request.json() (app/_lib/request-body.ts:106-124 is used by only 47).
body:
## Summary
Give the refusal half of the error vocabulary a throwable form. A `Refusal` class (code, status, optional extra and operator detail) that any lib module can throw, plus one responder `answerFailure(err, route, storeCode)` that answers a Refusal with `jsonRefusal` and everything else with `safeJsonError`. Migrate the five lib error classes that already carry, or should carry, a refusal code, and collapse their six routes' catch blocks to one line.

## Description
The response vocabulary in `app/_lib/api-response.ts` is one authority, but the classification (is this failure a decision or an accident?) is re-made at every route. Lib modules that know the answer have grown three different hand-made shapes for it: `AtsConnectionError`/`AtsFieldMapError` carry `code: RefusalErrorCode`, `PortabilityError` carries code + status, and `PostingClosedError` carries nothing, so three routes each re-type `jsonRefusal("POSTING_CLOSED", 410)`. Two more modules (`matrix-error-code.ts`, `extract-text`'s `ExtractAnswer`) wrote their own refusal-vs-store classifiers. Across the API there are 30 distinct `instanceof …Error` checks. When a route gets the mapping wrong, the failure is a leak: `jobs/[id]/candidates` forwards `PipelineError.message` and sits on the leak ceiling.

The error-handling golden path puts it plainly: one classification, produced once, consumed by every door. Structured propagation says the layer where the failure starts attaches the category, and the deciding layer only routes it. `Refusal` is that category, attached where it is born. `answerFailure` is the single router. A tree guard stops a new code-carrying error class from extending bare `Error`, so the pattern cannot fork again.

This is not the pending "Split the STORE_ERRORS / REFUSAL_ERRORS catalogs" item. That item moves the catalogs; this card changes how failures travel up to them. Both can land independently.

## Flow
1. `app/_lib/refusal.ts` (pure, no next/server): `class Refusal extends Error { code: RefusalErrorCode; status: number; extra?; detail? }`; the default message is `REFUSAL_ERRORS[code]`.
2. `api-response.ts`: `answerFailure(err, route, storeCode)`. A Refusal logs its detail at info level and returns `jsonRefusal(code, status, extra)`. Anything else returns `safeJsonError(err, route, storeCode)`.
3. Re-base `PostingClosedError` (POSTING_CLOSED/410), `PortabilityError`, `AtsConnectionError` (+Stale 409) and `AtsFieldMapError` on Refusal. Names and constructor signatures stay the same.
4. Collapse the catches in devcase inbound/submit/session-submit, workspace export/import and ats/connections (the stale branch stays, because it needs the live row). Update the one regex pin in import-body-limit.test.ts.
5. Add the tree guard in refusal.test.ts. Document the shape in api-contracts.md §1.1.

## Expected impact
A lib author who knows a failure is a decision throws a Refusal, and every route that reaches it answers correctly without new mapping code. Six catch blocks lose their bespoke branches. Five classes share one shape instead of three. A code-carrying error that bypasses the shape now turns the build red. Later leak burn-downs, such as the jobs/candidates PipelineError or the analytics raw-error KPI d0aabb73, become a one-line re-base of the error class rather than per-route surgery. The wire is unchanged: the same codes, statuses and bodies go out.

## Evaluation
Claim: refusal-vs-store classification is made once, at the throw site, and routed by one responder.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (no Refusal, no answerFailure, no tree guard).
After: 8 of 8.
Method: node:test cases in app/_lib/refusal.test.ts plus the updated source pins, run under `npm run test:unit`, then the integration gate (tsc, lint, i18n:check, api:check, test:unit).
Result: pending build.
Gate: architecture.

title: Limiter refusals that say when: shared Retry-After from the window's own state
acceptance: rateLimitRetryAfterMs(key, now): with {limit: 2, windowMs: 60_000}, two hits at t0 and a refused third hit, reading at t0+15_000 -> 45_000; an unknown key -> null; reading at t0+60_000 (window reset) -> null
Read without disturbing: calling rateLimitRetryAfterMs(key) 100 times does not change the outcome of the next rateLimit(key, opts) call, and does not create an entry for an unknown key

withRetryAfter(res, 45_001, 60_000) sets header Retry-After: "46"; remainingMs 200 -> "1" (never 0); remainingMs 600_000 with windowMs 60_000 -> "60" (capped at the window); remainingMs null / 0 / NaN / negative -> NO Retry-After header (a fabricated wait is worse than none)

jsonThrottled(retryAfterMs, windowMs) -> status 429, body { error: REFUSAL_ERRORS.TOO_MANY_REQUESTS, code: "TOO_MANY_REQUESTS", retryAfterSeconds: N } with N equal to the Retry-After header; when retryAfterMs is null the body has no retryAfterSeconds and there is no header

Machine doors: after exhausting the pinned budget on billing/webhook, channels/inbound/[token], channels/webhooks/[token], agents/report/[token] and devcase/inbound (both the burst and daily buckets), the next 429 carries Retry-After <= that bucket's window (behavioural drive of the real limiter in rate-limit-contract.test.ts)

Tree rule in rate-limit-contract.test.ts: 0 files under app/api call headers.set("retry-after"|"Retry-After", ...) directly; login, invite, tts and stt delegate to withRetryAfter, and their existing header semantics hold (login: longer of the two tripped windows, capped; tts/stt: header only when the engine gave a wait)

rateLimitRefusalStats() after 3 refusals on `inbound:<tok>:local` and 1 on `billing-webhook:local` -> { inbound: 3, "billing-webhook": 1 }; admissions are not counted; keys are reduced to the prefix before the first ':' so no token or IP reaches /api/ops, which exposes the map as `rateLimitRefusals`
premise: app/_lib/rate-limit.ts:21-35 — rateLimit() returns a bare boolean; the window's resetAt (rate-limit.ts:13, `type Window = { count: number; resetAt: number }`) is known at refusal time and thrown away.

147 non-test call sites answer `jsonRefusal("TOO_MANY_REQUESTS", 429)` (grep); only 4 routes send Retry-After, and each hand-rolls it: app/api/auth/login/route.ts:47-58, app/api/invite/[token]/route.ts:37-45 (the same clamp logic, copied), app/api/tts/route.ts:52-58 and app/api/stt/route.ts:77. None of the four gets its figure from the shared limiter.

Machine callers that honour Retry-After are refused with no wait: app/api/billing/webhook/route.ts:43-45 (Polar retries deliveries), app/api/channels/inbound/[token]/route.ts:66-67 (third-party boards / Zapier relays), app/api/channels/webhooks/[token]/route.ts:26-27, app/api/agents/report/[token]/route.ts:168-169, app/api/devcase/inbound/route.ts:91-96.

app/api/tts/route.ts:42-50 documents why the helper was not shared: rate-limit-contract.test.ts pins the limiter call and its refusal as a source pair (app/api/rate-limit-contract.test.ts:2146-2159 checks the 400 chars after the rateLimit call for `jsonRefusal("TOO_MANY_REQUESTS", 429)`), so a shared responder has to be taught to the contract rather than hidden from it.

app/api/ops/route.ts:122-126 already exposes in-process counters (schedule reconcile/no-slot, afterResponseFailures) to the operator; the limiter has no counter at all, so an operator cannot tell which door is refusing.

Open leftover adopted: `.claude/scan-history/leftover-develop-2026-09-17.jsonl:590` — "Return limiter resetAt and send retryAfterSeconds" (shared-api-utilities, M, impact 9). It does not appear in either low-risk-drain-2026-09-22*-results.jsonl, so it is open. This card widens it with the tree rule over the hand-rolled headers and the operator counter, which is what moves it past the drain's risk band.
rollback: rateLimit()'s boolean signature and every one of the ~140 untouched call sites stay as they are. throttle-response.ts is a new leaf. Each migrated route is its own commit that swaps `jsonRefusal("TOO_MANY_REQUESTS", 429)` for `jsonThrottled(...)` (plus a hoisted key const), and the contract rows move with it, so reverting any route commit restores the old pair and its old pin. The ops field is additive JSON. The series reverts in any order.
runner_up: A behavioural route driver in app/_lib/testing (callRoute(handler, {method, body, headers, params}) on the next-server shim) to replace source-regex contracts: 58 test files read route.ts source, 104 import handlers, 16 re-declare a local post() builder.
body:
## Summary
Make the shared limiter's 429 say when to come back. Add a non-consuming `rateLimitRetryAfterMs(key)` read of the window the limiter already keeps. Add one clamp-and-header rule (`withRetryAfter`, `jsonThrottled`) in a new leaf module and route the four hand-rolled Retry-After sites through it. Move the five machine-called public doors onto it, and give the operator a per-family refusal counter on /api/ops. This adopts the open leftover "Return limiter resetAt and send retryAfterSeconds".

## Description
`rateLimit()` knows the exact instant a refused caller would be admitted: `resetAt` sits on the window it just checked. It returns `false` and discards it. So 147 throttled doors answer a 429 with no wait. The four routes that do send Retry-After (login, invite, tts, stt) each wrote their own clamp, and login and invite are copies of each other. The refusal-contract technique holds that a refusal is the limiter's main interface: it should carry a retry-after computed from the arithmetic that refused, never a constant, and it should carry nothing when there is no honest figure. The callers that act on this are machines: Polar's webhook redelivery, inbound lead relays, agent reports, devcase intake. Today they probe blind, and every probe is another refusal. The limit-observability technique adds the operator's side: a limiter with no readout has two states, silent and on fire.

The contract test pins each limiter call to its refusal on purpose (tts/route.ts:42-50 explains why). The card therefore extends the pin to accept `jsonThrottled(` right after the pinned `rateLimit(` call, and adds a tree rule that no route sets Retry-After by hand. The chokepoint gets stronger, not weaker.

## Flow
1. `rate-limit.ts`: add `rateLimitRetryAfterMs(key, now?)` (reads the window, never creates or counts) and `rateLimitRefusalStats()` (refusals per key prefix before ':'). `rateLimit()` keeps its signature.
2. `app/_lib/throttle-response.ts`: `withRetryAfter(res, remainingMs, windowMs)` (ceil, at least 1, at most the window, omitted when not finite or not positive) and `jsonThrottled(retryAfterMs, windowMs)` (jsonRefusal TOO_MANY_REQUESTS plus `retryAfterSeconds` data plus the header).
3. Route login/invite (persisted-throttle figure) and tts/stt (engine figure) through withRetryAfter. Their semantics stay the same.
4. Migrate billing/webhook, channels/inbound/[token], channels/webhooks/[token], agents/report/[token] and devcase/inbound (burst and daily) to `jsonThrottled(rateLimitRetryAfterMs(key), OPTS.windowMs)`, and update their contract rows and pins.
5. Add the tree rule to rate-limit-contract.test.ts. Add `rateLimitRefusals` to /api/ops. Document the header in api-contracts.md §1.4.

## Expected impact
Machine callers of five public doors get a truthful Retry-After and back off once instead of hammering. The four hand-rolled clamps become one rule with one set of tests. The operator can see which door family is refusing. The remaining ~140 human-facing doors can adopt the same responder one line at a time, since the contract already accepts it. No catalog change is needed: the code stays TOO_MANY_REQUESTS and `retryAfterSeconds` is extra data, which clients ignore until they choose to render it.

## Evaluation
Claim: every refusal from the shared limiter on the migrated doors carries a retry-after derived from the window that refused, and no route hand-rolls the header.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (no retry read, no shared responder, 4 hand-rolled headers, no refusal counter).
After: 7 of 7.
Method: node:test in app/_lib/rate-limit.test.ts plus the behavioural drive and tree rule in app/api/rate-limit-contract.test.ts, run under `npm run test:unit`, then the integration gate (tsc, lint, api:check, test:unit).
Result: pending build.
Gate: contract.
